subject: Entropy seeding & HSM handshake — design review for BYOK in VPC/on-prem
messages:
From: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@bankcorp.com>
To: ava_chen
Cc: connor_obrien
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial questions — BYOK/HSM handshake for private deployment

Ava / Connor,

Thanks for the helpful pre-call yesterday. As we prep for the internal review at BankCorp, security asked for a short write-up of how Redwood supports customer-owned keys (BYOK) for a private deployment in our VPC. A few specific questions they want covered:

- Do you support HSM-backed key material with remote attestation (e.g., TPM attestation / HSM certificate chains)?
- What is the entropy source and seeding model when keys are generated on-prem vs when Redwood imports wrapped keys?
- Can we enforce customer-only key-import (no Redwood custodial copy) and still get operational features like rotation triggers and key versioning?
- Operator access model: how are key-operator privileges segmented (Redwood ops vs customer on-call) and what audit trails exist?

I attached a spreadsheet with the questions (bankcorp_kms_questions.xlsx). Will Harper from our infra team may join the design call — copying him on the thread. Security also asks about disaster recovery: if a customer loses access to their on-prem keys, what are the recovery options?

Would appreciate a short design note or diagram before our architecture review next week.

Regards,
Jorge
Head of Infrastructure Security
BankCorp


From: ava_chen
To: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@bankcorp.com>
Cc: connor_obrien
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial questions — BYOK/HSM handshake for private deployment

Jorge — thanks for the list, very helpful. I pulled together a short proposal (attached: entropy-seeding-proposal.pdf) and an ops checklist (hsm-ops-checklist.md) — high level points below. Happy to walk through on a call and tighten details for BankCorp's compliance team.

Top-level options we recommend (choose per-account):

1) Customer-managed HSM (preferred for high-regulatory):
   - Bank provides an HSM in their environment (or a customer-allocated cloud HSM instance). Redwood performs a remote attestation flow (KMIP or cloud provider attestation) and registers the HSM certificate chain.
   - Keys are generated on the customer HSM when required (no plaintext leaves the HSM). Redwood stores only key references and metadata (KID, version, policy).
   - Entropy: sourced from the HSM's TRNG. We record HSM firmware version and attestation evidence in the audit log.

2) BYOK import with offline-wrapping:
   - Customer generates keys with their HSM and exports a wrapped key blob (using a mutually-agreed wrapping key). The blob is imported via a signed import API — Redwood accepts the wrapped blob and never keeps the unwrapped key.
   - Entropy provenance is asserted by the importer via signed attestation and chain-of-custody metadata.

3) Redwood-managed HSM with customer-controlled wrapping (hybrid):
   - For customers who want Redwood to host; we offer a hardware-backed KMS in a dedicated tenant. Customer supplies an external root-wrapping key (BYOK root) that we use to encrypt HSM-generated keys; Redwood operational staff cannot unseal application keys without the customer's wrapping key being present.

Rotation and operational considerations:
- Rotation can be automated via policy (time-based or usage-based) but requires customer-supplied wrapping material or an approved attestation flow for re-encryption.
- We support emergency rotation via a pre-agreed escrow-free handoff: the customer provides a one-time unwrapping credential in an out-of-band channel; this is recorded in audit logs and requires multi-party approvals.
- Operator access: Redwood enforces least-privilege: HSM transport and import APIs require mTLS + signed requests, plus RBAC for key management actions. All operator actions are logged with immutable audit entries (hash-chained log records).

Disaster recovery options (if on-prem keys are lost):
- If the customer has escrowed a wrapped backup (recommended): Redwood can re-import a valid wrapped backup after multi-sig approval.
- If no backup exists and no escrow is allowed: application recovery requires re-issuing new keys and rotating application secrets; we provide a migration plan but ciphertext encrypted under the old key will be unrecoverable.

Next steps I propose:
- Short call (30 min) to validate BankCorp requirements and identify which option they need.
- Share the attached proposal and checklist with their compliance team for triage.

Attachments: entropy-seeding-proposal.pdf, hsm-ops-checklist.md

Best,
Ava Chen
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ava@redwood.ai


From: connor_obrien
To: ava_chen, Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@bankcorp.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 08:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial questions — BYOK/HSM handshake for private deployment

Quick follow-up with operational guardrails and suggested defaults:

- Default for FFIEC/regulatory customers: customer-managed HSM (option 1). Don't default to Redwood-managed unless expressly permitted.
- Entropy verification: include an HSM-fingerprint and attestation nonce in the initial registration flow. Store the attestation artifact (cert + nonce) in the audit bundle per-account.
- Rotation window: suggest 90-180 days for wrapping keys; application keys can be longer depending on data classification. Provide automatic rotation but require customer acknowledgement for root-wrapping key changes.
- Operator separation: Redwood ops must not hold the unwrapping material for tenants that opt-out of escrow. Add an emergency access workflow that requires: (a) customer SRE approval, (b) two Redwood manager approvals, (c) time-delayed ticket and immutable audit record.
- Monitoring: push HSM attestation failures and key-lifecycle events to the customer's SIEM via syslog/CloudEvent.

One ask for the proposal doc: clarify the format of the wrapped blob and the exact KDF/AEAD construction we accept for imports (so BankCorp can validate with their HSM vendor). I linked a short spec in the checklist; will you add the crypto primitive choices?

—Connor
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference


From: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@bankcorp.com>

Ava / Connor — this looks great, thanks for the clear options. A few quick notes from security and next steps:

- Security confirmed they will only accept option 1 (customer-managed HSM) or option 2 with an explicit KDF/AEAD profile (they listed AES-GCM-SIV + HKDF-SHA256 as acceptable). Please include that in the import spec.
- We want the attestation artifact retained for 7 years for audit — is that feasible?
- Can you send the diagram to our architecture Slack and propose 2 times for a 30-min sync? We also want to invite our vendor (EdgeCloud) for a short pairing session on the KMIP attestation.
- For recovery: BankCorp cannot use custodial escrow except under emergency contractual exception. Please outline the emergency access ticket template and the approvals you mentioned in a formal Annex.

I'll route the spreadsheet to procurement and schedule the sync once we have a refined import format.

Thanks,
Jorge
